badges.name: Membership Badge
badges.purpose: To help new members know the Scout Movement and the Rover Scout Section, and to understand and accept the Scout Promise and Scout Law
badges.description: Training and assessment are arranged by the Crew Management Committee. The badge is approved and presented by the Rover Scout Leader upon recommendation by the Chairperson of the Crew Management Committee. Two Crew activities taken part in while obtaining the "Rover Scout Link Badge" can be counted towards this requirement.

items.name: Take part in the Crew activities for at least 3 times. One of which should be an activity organised by the Crew or the Group and one of which should be an outdoor or sea activity.
items.detail: Activities organised by the Crew or the Group include variety show, joint-group activity, open day etc. Outdoor activities include trip, camping, campfire, outdoor Crew meeting etc. Sea activities include swimming, rowing, canoeing training or activities etc.

segments.name: Understanding
segments.desc: National Flag and Emblem, and the Scout Movement

items.name: Identify the national flag and national emblem of the People's Republic of China and understand their meanings.
items.detail: The Five-star Red Flag and the national emblem of the People's Republic of China

items.name: Identify the regional flag and regional emblem of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and understand their meanings.
items.detail: The Bauhinia regional flag and regional emblem

items.name: Understand the meaning of the national anthem of the People's Republic of China and be able to sing it by memory.
items.detail: The March of the Volunteers

items.name: Understand the Scout Movement in Hong Kong and the World Scout Movement.
items.detail: History of the development of the Scout Movement in Hong Kong; introduction of each Section from the Grasshopper Section to the Rover Scout Section; history of the founder of the World Scout Movement, its development and current situations.

items.name: Know the rite to the National Flag and Emblem, Regional Flag and Emblem, and National Anthem.
items.detail: Regulations for the use and display of the National Flag and Emblem and the Regional Flag and Emblem

items.name: Demonstrate how to raise the National Flag and the Regional Flag.
items.detail: Work in pairs; flags must not touch the ground

items.name: Be able to identify the uniforms of each Section. Know the Rover Scout uniform and the correct methods of wearing different badges and their positions.
items.detail: Refer to the uniform manual

items.name: Be able to know the uniform for leaders and distinguish different ranks for leaders.
items.detail: Leader uniform and ranks

items.name: Be able to use and understand the Scout Salute, the Scout Hand Shake and the Scout Sign; know the basic formation commands and signs, and basic foot drill.
items.detail: Commands and movements of static drills and marching; basic foot drill training

items.name: Understand the ceremonies of flag raising, flag lowering and investiture.
items.detail: Investiture ceremony and flag lowering ceremony

items.name: Understand and accept the Scout Promise and Scout Law: be able to recite them, know their meanings, and be willing to practise them in daily life.
items.detail: "On my honour, I promise that I will do my best to do my duty to God and to my Country, to help other people and to keep the Scout Law."

items.name: Complete the "Safe from Harm Online Self-Learning Course" (mandatory from 1 July 2025).
items.detail: To help members understand how to recognise, prevent and act towards inappropriate behaviour, ensuring Scouting activities are carried out in a safe environment. Course: https://sfh.scout.org.hk

badges.name: Rover Scout Epaulettes
badges.purpose: To provide a platform for new Rover Scouts to experience activities and learn basic Scoutcraft, and to serve as a way for Rover Scouts from different backgrounds to interact with each other
badges.description: Upon approval and recommendation by the Rover Scout Leader, the Epaulettes are endorsed and issued by the District Rover Scout Leader / Assistant District Commissioner (Rover Scouts) / Assistant Regional Headquarters Commissioner (Rover Scouts) / Regional Headquarters Commissioner (Rover Scouts). Rover Scouts who have completed the Rover Scout Link Badge upon being invested into the Rover Scout Section are regarded as having completed this assessment.

items.name: Complete a Rover Scout Introductory Course recognised by the Association Headquarters / Regions / District, or complete equivalent items.
items.detail: Appendix: Overview of the Rover Scout Introductory Course. Target: Rover Scouts; Venture Scouts aged 17 or above; non-Scouts aged 18 or above interested in Rover Scouting. Contents: history and evolution of Rover Scouting, training aims, Crew organisation and administration, Award scheme, Rover Scout skills, activity experiences, and reading and sharing a Scout Movement book. An overnight activity is suggested. A Rover Scout Introductory Course completed before becoming a Rover Scout can fulfil this requirement. Rover Scouts who have completed the Rover Scout Link Badge upon being invested into the Rover Scout Section are regarded as having completed the Epaulettes assessment.

badges.name: Rover Scout Award
badges.purpose: The Rover Scout Award is awarded when the member completes 4 of the 7 assessment components. All seven components can be conducted simultaneously
badges.description: The seven components — Dedication, Scoutcraft, Volunteerism, Global Vision, Tenacity, Mental and Physical Wellness, and Intrepidity — are closely aligned with the educational goal of "Service-Mindedness and Global Vision". Rover Scouts must plan their personal progress and gain approval from the affiliated Headquarters Commissioner (Rover Scouts) by submitting the "Application for Assessment of the Rover Scout Award and Baden-Powell Award" before the initiation of the assessment. Average completion time: 12-18 months. Rover Scout Award: after completing four components, confirmed and recommended by the District, endorsed and issued by the Region, and confirmed and issued by the Association Headquarters (Scheme p.19).

segments.name: Dedication
segments.desc: Wood Badge training and Group service

items.name: Complete Wood Badge Framework Stage 1 - Fundamentals of Scouting Course (Module 1A & 1B) or equivalent items.
items.detail: If a Rover Scout completes any of the Wood Badge trainings before the commencement of this assessment, the relevant completed parts will be recognised retrospectively.

items.name: Complete Wood Badge Framework Stage 2 - Sectional Training Methods Course (Module 2A & 2B) and In-Service Mentorship, or equivalent item; or serve within a Scout Group for at least 52 hours in at least 12 months.
items.detail: Rover Scouts can wear the Gilwell Woggle after completing the Wood Badge Framework Stage 2 or equivalent items.

segments.name: Scoutcraft
segments.desc: Traditional scoutcraft + instructor training + foot drill

items.name: Complete one of the following "traditional scoutcraft" training courses or the equivalent: (i) Expedition Course; (ii) Campcraft Course; or (iii) Pioneering Course.
items.detail: If a Rover Scout has already completed all Traditional Scoutcraft training courses (or equivalent) before undertaking this assessment, or is unable to complete the training due to reasonable circumstances, item 1 may be fulfilled by completing one other Leader Skills Training Course listed in the Wood Badge Training System. However, the course chosen cannot be the First Aid Certificate Course, Knotting Course, or Map Reading Course.

items.name: Complete one training course for instructors/assessors listed on the website of the Programme Branch.
items.detail: e.g. Rope Course Instructor, Challenge Course Instructor, etc.

items.name: Complete the Chinese Foot Drill Workshop and one of the following courses: (i) Basic Etiquette and Foot Drill Course; or (ii) Foot Drill Basic Course.
items.detail: If a Rover Scout has already completed the "Scout Foot Drill Basic Course", it is regarded as having fulfilled the Foot Drill Basic Course listed in item (ii).

segments.name: Volunteerism
segments.desc: First aid + Scouts of the World Award

items.name: Hold a valid First Aid Certificate issued by the Scout Association of Hong Kong, or other certificates of 30-hour First Aid courses recognised by the Labour Department in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Chapter 509). The certificate must still be valid when submitting the Baden-Powell Award application.
items.detail: e.g. St. John Ambulance or Hong Kong Red Cross 30-hour First Aid courses

items.name: Complete the "Scouts of the World Award Discovery Workshop".
items.detail: A Discovery Workshop recognised by the Programme Branch

items.name: Complete the Voluntary Service of the "Scouts of the World Award", or equivalent service.
items.detail: Organise and complete a period of voluntary service of at least 14 days in group. This item must be completed after the commencement of this assessment.
items.tip: Discovery + Voluntary Service are the two parts of the Scouts of the World Award

segments.name: Global Vision
segments.desc: Daily Interactions or International Exchange (complete Item A or B)

items.name: A) Daily Interactions - choose an exchange or cooperation task with people of different nationalities during group activities held on campus, office and/or workplace. Carry out a research regarding the experience for not less than 6 months, and share the experience and research with others.
items.detail: The method of sharing can be formulated after discussion with the corresponding Headquarters Commissioner (Rover Scouts).

items.name: B) International Exchange - participate in one international exchange programme that lasts for at least "5 days and 4 nights", and share your experience upon completion of the programme.
items.detail: Examples: World Scout Jamboree, World Scout Moot, World Scout Conference, APR Scout Conference, Scout Group Exchange Tour, international or Asia youth exchange programme, or an exchange tour in the Belt and Road Initiative Countries. The location is recommended to be outside Hong Kong and the activity must comprise international exchange; activities that are purely for tourism purposes cannot be regarded as an international exchange. The method of sharing can be formulated after discussion with the corresponding Headquarters Commissioner (Rover Scouts).
items.tip: Recommended outside Hong Kong; must include international exchange elements

segments.formSummary: ☐ A: Daily Interactions　☐ B: International Exchange

segments.name: Tenacity
segments.desc: 52 hours in 12 months - non-sports interest or skill

items.name: Choose a non-sports activity, interest or skill. Further develop or participate in this activity/interest/skill for no less than 52 hours within no less than 12 months, demonstrating progress in it (e.g. deeper understanding or mastering an appropriate level).
items.detail: Examples: Drone Piloting, Rope Access/Rescue Techniques, Generative AI Application, Robotics application, eSports, Motorsport, Dirt bike, Astrology, Cosmetics, Opera, Amateur Radio, 3D printing, Card games, Coffee Brewing or foaming, Wine Tasting or Cocktail Mixing, research on culture/economics/history/science, etc.

segments.name: Mental and Physical Wellness

items.name: Complete one or more certificates from "The Friendly Community - SOUL Keeper Scheme" or other mental-health-related certificates/courses, and carry out no less than 10 hours of related services, with more than 50 hours of training and service in total.
items.detail: Certificates or courses may fall under "Prevention" (understanding and promoting mental health) and/or "Intervention" (identifying mental health issues and providing support). Course hours are recognised retrospectively; the related service must be carried out after commencing this assessment.

items.name: Learn or participate in one physical activity, further developing or participating in it for no less than 52 hours within no less than 12 months, demonstrating sustained progress.
items.detail: Examples: Inline skating, Artistic Cycling, Skateboarding, Street dance, Surfing, Skiing, Ice-skating, Rock climbing, Bodybuilding, Lifesaving (e.g. beach rescue, canoe rescue, rescue diver), etc.

segments.formLabel: Mental and Physical Wellness 身心健康

segments.name: Intrepidity
segments.desc: Wilderness Challenge or Personal Challenge (complete Item A or B)

items.name: A) Wilderness Challenge - conduct an expedition journey of "3 days and 2 nights" or more with other Rover Scouts and/or Venture Scouts. Submit an expedition plan before the journey, and an expedition log and project log after the journey. Complete recognised expedition training before starting.
items.detail: The journey should be done as a team of 3 to 6 members (mixed-gender teams need at least two members of each gender); all participating members must never have conducted a "3 days and 2 nights" expedition assessment; at least 21 hours of related activities including the expedition journey process, achieving the purpose of the journey, campcraft, cooking and expedition projects; each member should take up some important roles and complete 2 projects together with the teammates. The assessment must be conducted by Senior Expedition Assessors or Expedition Assessors recognised by the Association Headquarters.

items.name: B) Personal Challenge - complete a challenge that has never been done before, to challenge oneself.
items.detail: Examples: Cross Harbour Race, triathlon, marathon, cycling expedition journey, overseas expedition journey, HKAYP Gold Award Adventurous Journey, Scout Wings, Scout Canopy Wings, completing 1 challenging charity activity e.g. Oxfam Trailwalker, etc. If a member has never completed a challenge of the same content or a higher level than the Wilderness Challenge, they must complete Item (A); conversely, if they have already completed such a challenge, they must complete Item (B) to embrace new challenges.
items.tip: Must be something never done before

segments.formSummary: ☐ A: Wilderness Challenge　☐ B: Personal Challenge

awardRule.note: Complete 4 of the 7 components to apply for the Rover Scout Award (Scheme p.19)

badges.name: Baden-Powell Award
badges.purpose: Complete all 7 assessment components; the District Commissioner and Regional Commissioner interview and recommend the member, and the Headquarters endorses and issues the award — the highest honour of the Rover Scout Section
badges.description: After completing the Rover Scout Award, continue and complete the remaining 3 components so that all 7 components are completed. Average completion time: 12 to 18 months.

segments.name: Baden-Powell Award - all 7 components
segments.desc: All 7 components of the Rover Scout Award must be completed before applying

items.name: Completed the Rover Scout Award (4 components) plus the remaining 3 components, i.e. all 7 components completed in total.
items.detail: The seven components: Dedication, Scoutcraft, Volunteerism, Global Vision, Tenacity, Mental and Physical Wellness, and Intrepidity.

items.name: Interview and recommendation by the District Commissioner and the Regional Commissioner.
items.detail: After completing all seven components, the District Commissioner and Regional Commissioner interview the member concerned and make recommendations.

items.name: Submit the application for the Baden-Powell Award; the Headquarters endorses and issues the award and certificate.
items.detail: Records and certificates must be submitted with the application.

otherBadges.name: Scouts of the World Award
otherBadges.desc: Complete the WOSM Scouts of the World Award: Discovery course and Voluntary Service.
otherBadges.detail: Attend the Discovery course recognised by the Programme Branch throughout; the action group organises and completes voluntary service equal to at least 14 full-time days of work, after the assessment has started. Issued by: Association Headquarters (Hong Kong Commissioner). Purchase: Scout Shop, with the original certificate issued by the authorised issuing authority.

otherBadges.name: Earth Tribe Programme
otherBadges.desc: Complete any one of the three Earth Tribe challenges: Plastic Tide Turners, Champions for Nature or Scouts Go Solar.
otherBadges.detail: Completing any one challenge makes you a member of the Earth Tribe. Wear the Earth Tribe Badge together with at least one challenge badge. When progressing to the next section, members must re-complete the relevant challenge(s), except Rover Scouts. Issued by: Programme Branch (Programme Commissioner).

otherBadges.name: Patrimonito Scout Badge
otherBadges.desc: Rover Scouts who complete the volunteer service of the Scouts of the World Award at UNESCO-recognised World Heritage Sites receive this badge together with the Scouts of the World Award.
otherBadges.detail: May be worn on the uniform. See the WOSM webpage for the Patrimonito Scout Badge. Issued by: Association Headquarters (Hong Kong Commissioner).

otherBadges.name: First Aid Badge
otherBadges.desc: Hold a valid 30-hour First Aid certificate.
otherBadges.detail: Upon attaining the First Aid Certificate issued by the Scout Association of Hong Kong, or a 30-hour First Aid course certificate recognised by the Labour Department under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509), the badge may be worn within the certificate validity period. Purchase: Scout Shop, with the original First Aid Certificate and the Rover Scout Record Book.

otherBadges.name: Scout Lifesaving Badge
otherBadges.desc: Attain the lifesaving qualification of the Hong Kong China Life Saving Society.
otherBadges.detail: May be worn within the validity period of the certificate. Course content is subject to Association Headquarters announcements. Purchase: Scout Shop, with the original Bronze Medallion (or higher) certificate and the Rover Scout Record Book.

otherBadges.name: Advance Aircrew Badge
otherBadges.desc: Upon attaining the Advance Aircrew Badge, Rover Scouts can wear this badge.
otherBadges.detail: May be worn together with the Coxswain Badge. Course content is subject to Association Headquarters announcements. Issued by the District, Region or Programme Branch officers listed in Chapter 5.

otherBadges.name: Coxswain Badge
otherBadges.desc: Upon attaining the Coxswain Badge, Rover Scouts can wear this badge.
otherBadges.detail: May be worn together with the Advance Aircrew Badge. Course content is subject to Association Headquarters announcements. Issued by the District, Region or Programme Branch officers listed in Chapter 5.

otherBadges.name: Scout Wings
otherBadges.desc: Upon attaining Scout Wings, Rover Scouts can wear the corresponding badge.
otherBadges.detail: Members can only wear either Scout Wings or Scout Canopy Wings. Course content is subject to Association Headquarters announcements. Issued by the Region or Programme Branch officers listed in Chapter 5.

otherBadges.name: Scout Canopy Wings
otherBadges.desc: Upon attaining Scout Canopy Wings, Rover Scouts can wear the corresponding badge.
otherBadges.detail: Members can only wear either Scout Wings or Scout Canopy Wings. Course content is subject to Association Headquarters announcements. Issued by the Region or Programme Branch officers listed in Chapter 5.

otherBadges.name: Active Citizenship Badge Series
otherBadges.desc: A series of challenges to encourage youth to participate actively in social affairs and develop leadership and teamwork.
otherBadges.detail: The series includes: Anti-Deception Badge, Child Protection Badge, Anti-Drug Badge, Community Emergency Responder Badge and Green Pioneer Badge. See the Active Citizenship Badge Series webpage. Issued by: Rover Scout Leader, District, Region or Programme Branch officers listed in Chapter 5.

otherBadges.name: Rover Scout Community Involvement Badge
otherBadges.desc: Complete a thematic workshop and a practical session on community involvement within 6 months.
otherBadges.detail: Part (A): complete a recognised thematic workshop (one or more of seven themes: Environmental Hygiene and Cleanliness; Anti-corruption; Fight Against Crime; Drug Education; Equal Opportunities; AIDS Prevention Education; Respect for Intellectual Property Rights). Part (B): practical session, including a personal logbook of the chosen theme, a group research study presented and reported, and a social service activity (assisting an HKSAR Government or registered social service organisation activity, or organising one) with proposal and report submitted to the assessor.

otherBadges.name: Rover Scout Religious Badge
otherBadges.desc: Choose one syllabus: Catholic, Christianity, Muslim, Confucianism, Buddhism or Taoism.
otherBadges.detail: The Rover Scout Leader may arrange a suitable person (such as a priest, chaplain or clergy) to assist with the assessments. Holders of the Venture Scout Religious Badge only need to complete the items specified in the syllabus. Wear in the same position as the Kiro Badge; only one of the two may be worn. Syllabus details are in Chapter 4 of the Scheme.

otherBadges.name: Kiro Badge
otherBadges.desc: Available only to baptised Catholic Scout members.
otherBadges.detail: For details, contact the Catholic Girl Guides and Scout Guild (info@catholicscout.org.hk). Wear in the same position as the Rover Scout Religious Badge; only one of the two may be worn.

otherBadges.name: HKAYP Gold Award
otherBadges.desc: Upon completing the Gold Award of The Hong Kong Award for Young People, you may wear it on the left sleeve of the uniform.
otherBadges.detail: If both Gold and Silver awards are held, only the Gold Award can be worn. When doing the Rover Scout Award and Baden-Powell Award assessments, the nature of the items can be considered to complete relevant HKAYP sections at the same time. Collection: gifted by the Programme Branch and distributed by the Scout Shop; present the original congratulation letter issued by the Region and the Rover Scout Record Book.

otherBadges.name: HKAYP Silver Award
otherBadges.desc: Upon completing the Silver Award of The Hong Kong Award for Young People, you may wear it on the left sleeve of the uniform.
otherBadges.detail: If both Gold and Silver awards are held, only the Gold Award can be worn. Collection: gifted by the Programme Branch and distributed by the Scout Shop; present the original congratulation letter issued by the Region and the Rover Scout Record Book.

trainingPlan.title: Training Scheme of the Rover Scout Section (5th Edition, effective 15 August 2026)
trainingPlan.purpose: The Rover Scout Section (aged 18-25; membership ends upon reaching 26) aims to connect and provide opportunities and support to young people who care about our society and are devoted to services, serving the Scout Movement and the community. Through a challenging award scheme, young people are encouraged to make personal progress and develop their potentials so as to become responsible and useful citizens in society.
method: Self-governing and self-programming: the Rover Scout Crew is self-governing, with the Crew Management Committee elected by members
Service-mindedness: develop personal potential and contribute to society through service
Global vision: cultivate global citizenship through international and cultural exchanges
Prospective leader training: Wood Badge training system + Group service, nurturing future leaders
Progressive awards: the 7 components can be conducted simultaneously; complete 4 to earn the Rover Scout Award, complete all 7 for the Baden-Powell Award
expected: Prospective leader capability: complete Wood Badge basic training and Group service
Passing on Scoutcraft: master traditional skills and instructor training, able to teach others
Spirit of service: first aid capability + Scouts of the World Award service, improving the community
Global vision: 6 months of daily cross-cultural interactions or a 5-day-4-night international exchange with sharing
Interest and skill (Tenacity): 12 months / 52 hours of sustained progress in a non-sports interest or skill
Mental and physical wellness: mental health training + 50 hours of service + 12 months / 52 hours of physical activity
Spirit of challenge: a 3-day-2-night wilderness expedition or a personal challenge never done before
trainingPlan.progressFlow: Membership Badge (3 activities) → Rover Scout Epaulettes (Introductory Course) → Rover Scout Award (4 of 7 components) → Baden-Powell Award (all 7 components)
trainingPlan.assessmentPrinciples: The 7 components can be conducted simultaneously. Rover Scouts must plan their personal progress and gain approval from the affiliated Headquarters Commissioner (Rover Scouts) by submitting the "Application for Assessment of the Rover Scout Award and Baden-Powell Award" before the initiation of the assessment. Parts completed beforehand can be recognised retrospectively.

legacyTransition.title: 第四版 → 第五版過渡安排
legacyTransition.source: 香港童軍總會通告 P022/2026 附件一「樂行童軍支部」
legacyTransition.enSource: Scout Association of Hong Kong Circular P022/2026, Annex 1 — Rover Scout Section
legacyTransition.policy: 2026年8月15日或之後宣誓的樂行童軍，必須按第五版考核。此前宣誓的成員可選擇按第五版考核，或沿用第四版，但須於2029年8月14日或以前完成；逾期未完成的獎章或項目須按第五版考核。選擇第五版者，可按下表把第四版已完成項目過渡至第五版；第五版所有項目備註仍適用。
legacyTransition.enPolicy: Rover Scouts invested on or after 15 August 2026 must be assessed under the 5th Edition. Those invested before that date may use the 5th Edition or continue under the 4th Edition, completing it by 14 August 2029. Any unfinished award or item after the deadline must be assessed under the 5th Edition. Members choosing the 5th Edition may transfer completed 4th Edition items as shown below; all 5th Edition notes still apply.
